135a6f7d72166abc72a0fc691651c47eb0ed1b5e.summary: CERT-FR report (17/07/2020) on the Dridex banking trojan. Dridex appeared in June 2014 as a fifth variant of Bugat with GameOverZeuS features. It runs on a peer-to-peer botnet and is operated under an affiliate model. The report traces its developers to Evil Corp, which grew out of the Business Club and the ZeuS family. It describes distribution through phishing, Emotet, FakeUpdates and exploit kits, and links Dridex to the BitPaymer and DoppelPaymer ransomware. Many links between groups are hedged as uncertain.

hedges: Without further evidence, it is only possible to confirm a close relationship between the groups linked to CraP2P.
Some sources say Evil Corp operates the CraP2P botnet, others say TA505; the report does not settle which.
It is not easy to tell whether TA544 is an affiliate of Dridex or only a distributor.
Dridex is manifestly operated (perhaps even developed) by at least one member of the Business Club, per the report.
Evil Corp is thought to have split in April 2019; the report says Doppel Spider may be a sub-group of Evil Corp.
The report says Bitpaymer development by Evil Corp is suggested by code similarities and shared prior compromise, not proven.
Dridex's maximum infection rate is considered to have been reached over 2015-2016.
Names in the report come from open sources and judicial documents that the report references.
